title: Explain-driven partitioning for sparse Console usage snapshot tables
creator: Ariana Cho
description:
Background: Console usage telemetry has highly skewed key distributions (a small set of routes and tenants generate the majority of invocations). Current weekly snapshots use static partition boundaries (date + tenant_bucket) which produce very large files for hot tenants and many tiny files for cold tenants. This causes inefficient scanning, imbalanced shuffle during downstream joins, and unpredictable query latency for dashboard queries and cost attribution jobs.

Objective: Design and implement an automated, explain-driven partitioning strategy for the curated Console usage snapshot tables (weekly and daily levels) that uses runtime query explain statistics and sample histograms to select partition boundaries and stabilization logic. Goals: reduce median query scan bytes by >=40% for common Console dashboards, reduce Spark shuffle skew on joins by >=30%, and keep data freshness and ingestion SLOs unchanged.
proposed_solution:
High level approach: 1) Collect query explain stats and table access patterns from Console query logs (most frequent predicates, group-bys, join keys). 2) Produce a small analysis job that samples the latest N weeks of raw invocation events and computes per-candidate-partition metrics: rows, cardinality, 95th-percentile-row-size, join-selectivity to route and tenant dimension tables. 3) Use a heuristics-driven optimizer that chooses either: a) hybrid partitioning (date + hot_tenant_id for top X tenants + tenant_bucket for the rest), or b) range partitioning by daily_invocation_quantiles for very hot routes, or c) coalesced micro-partitioning with column-level bloom filters for high-cardinality joins. 4) Persist the chosen layout as a partition policy record (metadata table) and use it in the snapshot ETL to create partitioned Parquet/Delta tables and targeted compaction rules.

Key characteristics: - Explain-driven: optimizer inputs include recent query plan predicates and filter frequency. - Adaptive: policy recomputes weekly and can pin partitions for 2-week stabilization to avoid churn. - Cost-aware: optimizer estimates scan and shuffle cost and prefers layouts that reduce expected bytes-read * query-frequency. - Implementation primitives: Spark sampling job, small metadata service (simple table in analytics DB), ETL template changes to apply partition policy and targeted compaction during ingestion.
schema_changes: No change to logical schema (we keep canonical invocation columns). Physical table changes: add a metadata column 'partition_policy_id' in internal metadata only (not surfaced to Console). Partitioning keys will vary by policy (examples: date, hot_tenant_id, tenant_bucket, route_quantile_range). We'll add a compact manifest table: console_ux.snapshots_partition_policies with fields stored in analytics config (policy_id, effective_start, effective_end, heuristics_blob) — this is recorded as a stringified JSON blob internally in the config table row. Downstream consumers see the same logical table and query via provided views that abstract partition layout.
materialization_plan:
Phases: 
1) Analysis stage (2 sprint work): implement sample-and-explain job, collect baseline metrics, run offline policy simulations.
2) Pilot (1 sprint): pick two tenant cohorts (one hot platform tenant, one SMB) and pilot hybrid partitioning for weekly snapshots, produce test snapshots and run dashboard query benchmark.
3) Rollout (2 sprints): implement ETL changes to apply policy, targeted compaction job, update Curated docs and runbooks.
4) Monitoring (ongoing): add SLOs for ingestion latency, job failures, and query latency regressions.

Operational notes: Use Delta/Parquet with Z-Ordering for route_id when applicable. Compaction job will be run offline during low-traffic windows and triggered by policy when small-file ratio >30% for a partition. ETL must be backwards compatible: write new snapshots as new table suffix _v2 until consumers migrate to the view.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarked dashboards (tenant top-10 routes and cost attribution) show >=40% reduction in median bytes scanned under the simulated query mix.
Weekly snapshot ETL completes within existing SLO (90th < 45 minutes) in pilot and full rollouts.
Compaction and targeted file sizing reduces number of files per hot-partition to under 100 for weekly tables.
No downstream consumer queries break when accessing the provided view abstraction; migration docs and a one-week dual-write strategy are published.
Policy recomputation job is scheduled and an alert exists if policy changes cause >10% increase in aggregate expected scan cost.
tasks: Build partition policy metadata table and simple REST read API for ETL
Add policy-driven partitioning logic to daily/weekly snapshot ETL templates
Pilot snapshots for two tenant cohorts and run query benchmarks
Implement targeted compaction job with safety checks and idempotency
Write migration runbooks, update curated table docs and Console knobs
comments: 2026-02-28 - Ariana Cho: Kickoff notes uploaded to Confluence. Initial sample runs show extreme skew: top 1% tenants account for ~62% of rows. Need to ensure compaction won't block producers.
2026-03-03 - Mateo Alvarez: Prototype of sample-and-explain finished. Added query predicate frequency extraction. Early heuristics favor hybrid partitioning for weekly summaries.
2026-03-07 - Sasha Ivanov: Reviewed pilot plan. Recommend adding bloom filter columns for join keys to evaluate join pruning effectiveness during queries.
2026-03-10 - Product (Imani Park): Confirmed acceptance criteria for dashboard latency improvements. Will provide a synthetic query mix to simulate PLG dashboard traffic.
notes_on_risks: Risks: frequent policy churn could cause compaction storms and high IO. To mitigate we freeze policies for 2 weeks by default and only allow emergency reconfiguration with a manual approval. Another risk is inaccurate query sampling causing suboptimal partitioning; we will keep a rollback plan and dual-write under _v2 suffix until consumers validate performance. There is also a potential cost trade-off between smaller scan bytes and increased metadata complexity — metricize and validate over three production cycles.
